scenario_description:
Objective: Keep Wednesday’s Willow Creek stencil-cleanup supply plan from creating avoidable runoff problems while preserving the volunteer shift.
Emerging Need: Donated degreaser is slated for the scrub tote, and a later stormwater notice confirms the work area has open inlet grates before the tote-sealing cutoff.
Decision Context: A stored cleanup rule identifies when liquid cleaners are unsafe near open drains, what lower-risk supplies are allowed, and when the tote can still be changed.
Consequence: Timely adjustment can remove the hazard before supplies leave staging; after sealing, the crew may arrive with materials that could carry detergent into the creek.

parameter.title: Willow Creek stencil-cleanup shift
parameter.description: Stencil repainting and litter sweep under Willow Creek Bridge; supply sort at the hub Tuesday afternoon.

parameter.subject: Willow Creek cleanup supply staging
parameter.body: For Wednesday's Willow Creek stencil repainting, the parks cart will be staged at the hub Tuesday. Volunteer leads may add donated supplies to the scrub tote until the cart is sealed at 16:30 Tuesday. Parks is not reviewing add-ons unless hub procedures require it.

parameter.content: I labeled the neighbor-donated citrus degreaser jugs for the Willow Creek stencil scrub tote with the brushes and gloves. I'm planning to seal that tote with the parks cart at 16:30.

parameter.subject: Willow Creek inlet-cover delay for Wednesday crews
parameter.body: This afternoon's inlet covers for the Willow Creek Bridge underpass are delayed until Thursday. Wednesday crews should assume the west-curb storm grates are open and draining toward the creek; avoid rinse water entering that curb line.

parameter.content: The Willow Creek scrub tote is sealed in the parks van now with the labeled degreaser and brushes. The van leaves the yard locked until the 07:30 crew pickup, so I won't be changing the contents tonight.

At the first stencil, a volunteer already applied the tote degreaser beside the open inlet before noticing the draining curb line. We have stopped that use now. Further cleanup advice may help, but the first unsafe application was not prevented.
